chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan, all of them, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

For the Mutamatti' (one who performs Umrah then Hajj), there are three circumambulations of the House and two Sa'ys between al-Safa and al-Marwah. So when he arrives in Mecca, he performs one circumambulation of the House and two rak'ahs at the Station of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and one Sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah. Then he shortens (his prayer) and has entered the state of Ihram for Umrah. And for him, for Hajj, there are two circumambulations and one Sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and he prays two rak'ahs at the Station of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) with each circumambulation of the House.

key_terms.اَلْمُتَمَتِّعُ: One who performs Umrah then Hajj, enjoying the blessings of both
key_terms.سَعْيٌ: Ritual walking between Safa and Marwah
key_terms.مَقَامُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: The Station of Ibrahim, a stone near the Kaaba
key_terms.يُقَصِّرُ: He shortens (the four-rak'ah prayer to two rak'ahs)

ai.seo_question: What are the ritual steps and number of circumambulations for a Mutamatti' performing Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the precise ritual structure of Hajj al-Tamattu', a practice highly favored in Shia jurisprudence for its spiritual accessibility. It clarifies that the pilgrim performs three distinct Tawafs and two Sa'ys, effectively merging the Umrah and Hajj rites while maintaining the state of Ihram until the final sacrifice, thereby distinguishing it from the Hanafi view of Hajj al-Qiran.
